screens_reviewed: Single iPad portrait scroll capture of the Execute tab in dark theme (screenshots/ipad/dark/05-execute.png): online status banner, place header card (Maple Library Plaza, SUBMITTED), Audits/Pending/Score metric row, a 'Report available' card, a floating Start survey / Open report CTA bar, and the bottom tab bar.
verdict: The screen reuses the shared primitives correctly (StatusBanner, Card, ScreenHeader, Badge, MetricCard, AppButton) and the content track is centered via getResponsiveContentContainerStyle, so it is structurally sound and theme-consistent. However it is essentially a scaled-up phone layout on the iPad canvas: a single narrow column with a large empty lower half and no master-detail/split adaptation, and the floating CTA bar bypasses the centered content track and the safe-area inset. These are real iPad-fit issues rather than broken UI.

critical_issues.issue: The floating CTA bar is positioned with left/right = layout.screenPaddingHorizontal only, so it spans the full viewport width minus the small screen padding. The scrolling content above it is centered and width-capped by getResponsiveContentContainerStyle (contentMaxWidth / adaptive gutters). On a wide iPad (landscape or >contentMaxWidth) the cards center to ~1040pt while the buttons stretch edge-to-edge, so the primary CTAs no longer align with the content column.
critical_issues.evidence: execute.tsx:187-190 sets left/right to layout.screenPaddingHorizontal; the ScrollView at execute.tsx:121 uses getResponsiveContentContainerStyle which applies alignSelf:'center'/maxWidth or adaptive gutters (lib/responsive-layout.ts:739-769).
critical_issues.fix: Wrap the floating XStack in a centered container that mirrors the content track: compute the same horizontal padding via getAdaptiveHorizontalPadding (or reuse getContentTrackInnerWidth from lib/responsive-layout.ts) and apply alignSelf:'center' + maxWidth = layout.contentMaxWidth so the buttons stay under the cards.

critical_issues.issue: The absolute CTA bar uses a hardcoded bottom: 16 and never reads useSafeAreaInsets().bottom. On iPads with a home indicator / gesture bar the buttons can sit under the indicator or too close to it; the bar also overlaps the tab bar region rather than clearing the home-indicator inset that the tab bar itself accounts for via getResponsiveTabBarLayout (lib/responsive-layout.ts:703-718).
critical_issues.evidence: execute.tsx:190 bottom: 16 is a fixed literal; the component imports no safe-area hook, unlike (tabs)/_layout.tsx:1457 which uses useSafeAreaInsets() for the tab bar.
critical_issues.fix: Read const insets = useSafeAreaInsets() and set bottom to insets.bottom + 16 (or tabBarLayout.height + insets.bottom) so the CTA clears the home indicator and tab bar on all iPad models.

improvements.suggestion: On iPad the screen renders as one narrow centered column with a large empty lower half (visible dead space below the 'Report available' card). This is a scaled-up phone layout. Consider an iPad master-detail / two-pane treatment for this tab: a place selector list on the left and the execute detail on the right, gated on layout.isTablet, reusing twoPaneGap/supportRailWidth tokens that already exist (lib/responsive-layout-tokens.ts:812-846). At minimum, use the available width to place the metric row and the offline/report card side-by-side.
improvements.evidence: Image shows roughly the bottom half empty; the route renders a single column with no isTablet branch (execute.tsx has no layout.isTablet / two-pane usage), while the layout tokens expose twoPaneGap and supportRailWidth for tablet panes.

improvements.suggestion: The three cards leave a tall empty region on iPad. Either constrain content into a more deliberate centered card group (vertically balanced) or add supporting context (recent activity, audit checklist preview) so the large canvas reads as intentional rather than unfilled.
improvements.evidence: Image: large dark area between the 'Report available' card and the CTA bar.

tamagui_notes: Shared primitives are used consistently: StatusBanner (execute.tsx:126), Card (128,162), ScreenHeader (129), Badge (134), MetricCard (154-159), AppButton (193,202) — no inline re-styling of these primitives was found, so the design_system_components_used contract is honored.

MetricCard row uses XStack gap="$3" flexWrap="wrap" (execute.tsx:153). With three MetricCard tiles each flex={1} (MetricCard.tsx:2168), at narrow widths a wrapped third tile would stretch full-width and break the 3-up grid; on the captured iPad width they fit one row, so this is latent, not visible here.

The CTA bar uses gap="$3" token spacing but positions itself with raw numeric left/right/bottom (execute.tsx:187-190) instead of the responsive content helper, which is the root of the alignment issue above.
platform_notes: Tab bar is correctly tablet-aware (getResponsiveTabBarLayout, isTablet icon size 22, label fontSize 12 in (tabs)/_layout.tsx:1448-1460), and content centering uses the iPad-aware getResponsiveContentContainerStyle — so the page is not entirely unadapted, but the body and CTA bar still read as phone-first.
No split-view / master-detail or multi-column adaptation for this tab despite the spare width and existing twoPaneGap/supportRailWidth tokens.
Content is width-constrained (good) but the CTA bar is not, so the two diverge at wide widths.
not_assessable: Exact contrast ratios; visually the green 'ONLINE' text, white title, and muted body all appear to meet AA on the dark surfaces, no clearly-failing pair identified.
Landscape / wide-iPad and split-view multitasking behavior (only one portrait capture provided) — the CTA-bar divergence is inferred from the width math, not seen.
Offline / pending-sync runtime states of StatusBanner and the Alert in openAuditForPlace (execute.tsx:227-230) are not shown.
Whether the lower empty area fills on taller content (different place status, drafts) cannot be judged from this single submitted-place capture.
score_rationale: Solid and ships-capable: correct, consistent use of every shared primitive, theme-correct, and content is centered via the responsive helper. It loses points for being a scaled-up phone layout on the iPad canvas (large empty region, no master-detail), a floating CTA bar that bypasses the centered content track, and a hardcoded bottom inset that ignores the iPad safe area — minor-to-moderate polish rather than broken UI.
